newsitem.title: HONG KONG: BEA says mortgage applications slow in Apr.
newsitem.headline: BEA says mortgage applications slow in Apr.

text.p: Bank of East Asia Ltd said that mortgage applications in April had slowed compared to the first three months of the year after the Hong Kong government announced measures to cool down rising property prices.
Daniel Wan, deputy general manager and chief financial officer of the bank, told reporters on Tuesday that the bank's mortgage lending had risen about 20 percent year on year in the first quarter.
The government announcement apparently affected the sentiment of home buyers, Wan said.
The bank's mortgage approval rate fell in April compared to the first quarter partly due to the slowdown in the number of applications, Wan said.
But the approval slowdown would not affect mortgage loan drawdowns until three months later, he said.
In a bid to speed up the flow of new housing supply to the market, the government last month extended the presale period for unfinished flats to 15 months before completion from 12 months.

It also required developers to put uncompleted flats on to the market within six months of receiving government approval for presales, and to release the flats in batches of at least 20 percent of the total number of approved units.
